topic.title: The ten-minute kitchen
topic.claim: Quick-delivery apps are slowly teaching you to stop keeping things at home, so you pay a fee every time you run out.
topic.moment: You order one packet of curd and a lemon at 9 pm because the fridge is empty again.

turn.actually: It moves your pantry into their dark store, and you pay rent on it each time you order.

topic.feeling: I'm spending more and planning less, and I can't tell where it went.
topic.villain: Handling, small-cart and late-night fees on top-up orders
topic.because: If your home stays empty, you come back daily. Daily small orders pay better than one big monthly one.
topic.payoff: What happens next: a whole generation that has never stocked a kitchen, renting one by the minute.
topic.behaviour: People order single items several times a week instead of a monthly stock-up.
topic.mechanism: Frequent small orders carry fees that one large order wouldn't.
topic.send_to: The flatmate who orders onions three times a week
topic.why_now: Quick commerce now sells almost everything, so the empty kitchen feels normal.

score.why: The 9pm curd-and-lemon order is every flatmate's habit, and 'renting your pantry by the minute' is a turn they haven't seen.
